1.right:
The conquest of the fortress of Constantinople in 1453 AD

(Reign of Mehmed II, 1453 - 1481)
In Peshawar, the Ghazi King Muhammad I also built for the conquest of Constantinople, known as the Anatolian Fortress. When Muhammad II ascended the throne, he also took on a similar ambition. To fulfill this desire, on the European side of the city, he prepared this in three months. Thousands of laborers were put to work. In these three months, he prepared this. On this large tower, a large cannon was placed, and four hundred soldiers were also appointed there, and the order was given that every passing ship should be taxed.
The construction of this fortress began in April 1453. Constantinople is triangular in shape. It is surrounded by water on two sides and land on one side. For this reason, a moat was prepared on the land side, which was one hundred yards wide. The width of the land is six miles. King Constantine, for the purpose of military operations and for the defense of this place, brought Greek soldiers to the moat on his own initiative and threw them at the Turks. But it soon became clear to him that this kind of work was very damaging. After a while, they attacked the fortress walls and from there they would bombard the enemy with arrows and cannonballs. On the other hand, the Turks took shelter from the digging of trenches and slowly advanced. The Sultan's cannon, which was very famous at that time, and the fire of other cannons spread to the fortress walls. And with the slow firing of these cannons, the battlefield was made like the Day of Judgment, and the weak points were broken. In addition, young Turks would go under the gates and reach the edge of the moat.

It is said that at that time, death was more desirable than life, as they had already sold themselves for gold. This was the reason why the mother's silence was cast upon herself. At this time, Sultan Muhammad used his intellect and came up with a strange plan:
He transported his light ships and Turkish equipment across the Bosphorus waters to the dry land, to the large part of the port. It was astonishing how, to transport ships on dry land, they built platforms, and on top of them, they placed logs and thick planks so that the ships could be moved. 7.right:
The wise sayings and words of Saad Zaghloul Pasha

Now, it is happening in the country that the news of the flood's emergence has spread, regarding this, I deemed it appropriate to translate a few wise words of the late Saad Zaghloul Pasha and present them to you, which are very good for the benefit of the field:-

1- Egypt wants complete independence, because this is the inherent right of nations. At this time, we are one reason, but the life of a nation cannot be disappointed by the fate of crushing another nation.

2- Being a humble subject of my nation seems very important to me. Claiming governance over it is a baseless attitude that is harmful.

3- A lover of freedom is not an extremist, because this is the benefit of love. A lover of slavery is an extremist, because slavery is the ultimate humiliation of the self.

4- The spirit of a nation is not something that disappears with laws, nor with oppression, nor with the great empires of the world.

5- O people of the country, it is the duty of all of you to specialize. Saad alone is not responsible; every person of the homeland is responsible.

6- If I say this, it is not my wish. It is not only that there is one nation in Egypt, and the Hindu is only the Egyptian nation.

7- Saad will always be alive even after death, because every Egyptian is Saad, rather, is more than Saad.

8- My life has no envy, no malice. In my soul, the national trust has not given way to anything.

9- Any place that claims to want freedom, has no minimal right.

is that a person, against the permission of his conscience, will
express misplaced praise and it is a clear matter

If flattery is done, a kind of pride and arrogance is born in him.

135.right:
Who are the Pashtuns?

It is stated in many authentic histories that the Pashtuns
are originally Copts and came from Egypt. When Hazrat Musa
Alaihis Salam gained victory over the Pharaoh, the King of Egypt,
many Copts became Muslims. However, one group among them
did not believe in God and His Messenger. Due to extreme
humiliation and ignorance, they left and came to India, and
settled in Koh-e-Sulaiman. Koh-e-Sulaiman is a famous mountain
near the side of the Wazir tribe. Ibn Battuta Maghribi has written
in his history, Tuhfat al-Nuzzar, that Hazrat Sulaiman
came through the path of Sistan to the end. When he was
on this mountain and looked down, India appeared dark to him.
He saw the people of this land as having a dark inner nature,
so he did not like this land. And because of this place...
...this mountain became famous as Koh-e-Sulaiman. When the Arabs
came to this land, they named this sect Sulaimani.
It is the people who live in the mountains of Koh-e-Sulaiman, not that
they are the children of Sulaiman. Abraha, who is
famous as Ashab al-Fil, when he came to destroy Makkah al-Mu'azzamah,
some of these people were also with him, who were killed in Makkah.
During the Caliphate of Amir al-Mu'minin Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him), in the year
when Abdullah bin Amir conquered Khorasan, these people became Muslims.

171.right:
Finding: Why did the British get upset?
The question is, for what reason did the sentiment of anger and resentment toward Afghans arise in the hearts of the British? In response to this, we must say that the British were aware of the pure hearts and good intentions of the Afghans, but they thought that the Afghans' pure hearts and good intentions did not mean they desired freedom, but rather that they harbored a desire for slavery in their hearts. When the Afghans breathed the air of freedom in their affairs and stood on their own feet, the British concluded that this was a rebellion against their authority, and therefore they embarked on a path of resentment and malice toward the Afghans. Now the question is, what is the reason for this? The answer is that in their hearts, there were such thoughts and suspicions that, due to the Afghans' thirst for freedom, they realized that the Afghans were no longer trapped in the shackles of slavery, and thus they tried to create obstacles in the path of their freedom, but this became a headache for them.

Independence Day in England and the Pashtun

There is no doubt that celebrating such an event in a civilized country like England, which results in opening the doors of freedom and independence for the people of a nation, is a matter of great joy and pride. We see that many efforts have been made in the capital of England to celebrate the Pashtun Independence Day. This day of joy, which holds a special place in the heart of every Pashtun, was celebrated in a grand manner by some scholars and politicians in London. The purpose of this gathering was not just to celebrate independence, but also to exchange a series of reforms and ideas for the unity and future prosperity of the Pashtuns. We hope that such gatherings will create unity among the Pashtuns and pave the way for their progress. During this meeting, many speakers emphasized that Pashtuns should look at their history and culture with respect and should not spare any effort in learning modern sciences.

If we do not remove our internal differences, it will be difficult for us to maintain our independence. At the end of the meeting, a resolution was also presented in which important points regarding the unity of Pashtuns, progress in the field of education, and raising political awareness were mentioned. According to the attendees, such meetings should be held continuously so that the spirit of love and service to the homeland can be kept alive in the minds of the new generation. Then his (Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him) right upon the Ummah is that you will act upon his Sunnah (peace be upon him) and you will be steadfast on his religion, and you will love him more than your own self and your own wealth.

(And) regarding him

And regarding him (Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him), you will show respect in his name and in his remembrance, and you will support and defend his Sunnah against innovation (and) disbelief and the words of sinners, and you will love his companions and his family, and you will say "peace be upon him" when his name is mentioned.
176.left:
43

And you will send blessings upon his name, and you will strive to follow his character (habits), and you will adorn yourself with his morals, and you will emulate him in his appearance and his conduct, and you will labor to spread his Sunnah.

(So) if you act upon this

Then if you act upon this and strive to follow his Sunnah for the sake of reforming yourself, the steadfastness of your religion, and the good of your worldly life, then you will be included in his (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him) intercession.

Regarding the condemnation of disbelief and sinful habits

In the condemnation of disbelief and sinful habits, condemning disbelief and sinful habits in contrast to his Sunnah, and striving to prohibit innovation and acts of disbelief, and to avoid evil deeds by following his Sunnah.

177.right:
Majority
Peshawar
Whoever makes any effort and endeavor in this path for the propagation of Islam and for the repulsion of its enemies is considered among the great servants of Islam and has a very great reward before God. In this regard, the courage of the Muslims of Pashtunkhwa is worthy of praise, as they have started some effort for the freedom and honor of their religion and their country, and the drops of heart's blood that have been shed in this path, their examples will be written in gold in history. Furthermore, the series of passion and fervor for the love of Islam is ongoing in the hearts of the Pashtun nation, so the result of this passion and fervor will surely come out with goodness, because the religion of Islam is based on truth and honesty, and falsehood cannot in any way confront the truth. Even though nowadays in the world, efforts are being made to suppress Islam with various means, God's promise is that the light of Islam will spread throughout the world. The status of the Muslims of Pashtunkhwa in their love for the religion is not hidden from anyone, and by the grace of God, the time has arrived when the Pashtuns will also become the leaders of other nations in the field of serving Islam, provided that they equip themselves with the ornament of knowledge and action, and maintain their unity, because without unity no nation can reach its goal. Pashtuns are very capable and intelligent among themselves, but they only need to recognize the necessity of unity. If the Pashtuns become united, they will do great things for Islam and will make the name of their country and nation shine in the world. It is the duty of every Pashtun to work day and night for the reform of their nation and the exaltation of the religion, and to confront the problems of the world with the power of their knowledge and wisdom. It is a prayer in the court of God Almighty that He may create the spirit of agreement and unity in the hearts of the Pashtun nation, grant them success in the path of serving the religion, and spread the light of their knowledge and understanding, so that they may live a life of honor and exaltation in the face of the world, Amen.
177.left:
The situation in Pashtunkhwa
Peshawar
Considering the situation in our Pashtunkhwa region, it can be said that the people's inclination towards knowledge and education has increased, which is a matter of happiness, because the foundation of a nation's progress is laid upon knowledge, and when a nation is adorned with the ornament of knowledge, then the way to liberation from all kinds of chains of slavery is found. Today, our Pashtun elders and youth are thinking about how to find a way to prevent the decline of their nation, so it is very necessary to make efforts to open madrasas and schools in societies, and in this regard, one should not refrain from any kind of sacrifice. In some areas, with the courage of the people, some associations have been formed to spread knowledge, whose work is worthy of praise, and there is a need for such efforts to be expanded in every region. Likewise, Pashtuns must also increase their efforts in the fields of agriculture and industry, because without economic power, no nation can stand on its own feet, so Pashtuns must also pay attention to learning modern sciences and industries. Along with this, reading history books is also very necessary so that they can be informed about the achievements of their ancestors, take lessons from them, and benefit from their experiences for their future. By the grace of God, a large number of scholars and poets exist in the land of Pashtunkhwa, who are striving for the awakening of the nation through their poetry and writings. If this work continues in an organized manner, then in a very short time, a major positive change will come to society. This is the time for work and action, so Pashtuns should not think that a nation is built only by words, rather action is a condition for every task. May God help the Pashtun nation on the path of knowledge and action.

The state of an old heart
(1)

I am sitting in a corner of the house like an old, old person. In front of me lies a book of sorrows, and on its face, the past years of my life are written as if someone had drawn a picture of a child's cry on glass with their fingers. On the wall is an old clock that goes tick-tock like an old heart. But my heart, which once bloomed like a flower in the time of tender youth, is today like a dry leaf that the wind blows in every direction. In the light of my eyes, the shadows of the images of those times appear, when life was a wild stream. Now everything has changed, and I am only searching in the dust of those memories that remain in the book of my life.

Now what should I say about her characteristics; she was a treasure of good qualities. She had a love for knowledge, as it was inherited from her ancestors. From what I have heard of her speech, there was such wisdom and knowledge in it that even many educated people would not be equal to her rank. Upon hearing her words, one would feel a strange peace, a peace that gave new life to the soul. When she would tell stories of the difficult and bitter days of her life, there was no complaint in them, but rather such an expression of contentment with Allah Almighty that a person would be left amazed. Her courage and patience were also matchless. Whenever a major problem or sorrow came into her life, she would prepare herself to face it with great calmness. These examples of her patience are still fresh in my mind. She used to say that life is a combined name for happiness and sorrow, and the duty of a Muslim is to express gratitude to Allah Almighty in both states.
179.left:

What should I say about her family life? She was an example of a mother and wife that everyone hopes for. In her home, there was an atmosphere of love, respect, and order. There was such a blessing in her hands that there was a special taste and love in her cooking and housework. Her upbringing of her children was such that we see it in very few homes these days. She did not just teach her children worldly lessons, but also taught them high standards of religion and morality. Her home was also always open to guests. Whenever a guest came to her home, they would greatly praise her humility and hospitality. In her presence, the house seemed like paradise. May God have mercy on her and make all her good deeds a provision for her in the afterlife. Her memory will always be alive in my heart, and her advice will be my guide in every moment of life.

183.right:
December 1920

Conditions

First, with the arrival of the new year and the completion of the third year since the martyrdom of Sardar Mohammad Khan, there were three days of mourning in Kabul. During these days, educational institutions, schools, and office operations were closed. Likewise, the procession of government officials and the public visiting the martyr's shrine to pay their respects continued. This day remains a memorial day in the history of the country.

Second, the Ministry of Education decided to change the curriculum for the new academic year. The purpose of this action is to replace old and worn-out books with new and modern sciences. The Minister said that we must compete with other nations of the world in the field of education and, for the progress of the country, we must turn the thoughts of the new generation toward scientific disciplines.

Third, the Ministry of Commerce announced that with the opening of the borders, the movement of goods would become easier. With the signing of trade agreements with neighboring countries, there will be a significant change in the country's economic situation. The government is trying to take special measures to increase exports and control imports so that domestic industry can grow.

213.right:
Pashtun

After reading the Pashtun issue dated the 7th of Jawza, a voice arose from my heart that will echo in my ears forever; it is that through which era of history my nation is passing, and what measures are being taken to overcome these calamities? I request permission to publish my thoughts through this Pashtun for that purpose, and I believe that there must be others like me who, upon seeing the decline of their nation, take up this pen with drops of their heart's blood. For the progress of the Pashtun, the Pashtun newspaper has the status of a torch that is very necessary for people to find their way in this darkness of shadows.

As an Afghan, I feel compelled to express some words for the brotherhood of my nation. Although I am a very weak person, I still cannot deny the power of the pen. If our nation takes a look at its past history, it will realize that the honor of the homeland has been protected at the cost of the life of every single Pashtun individual. But today, in what state are we living in our own homeland? It is a place of regret that we are afflicted with various calamities at the hands of the enemies of our homeland. Whether it is a lack of education or the result of our disunity, for this reason, the Pashtun is left behind in every kind of progress today.
213.left:
Pashtun

For this reason, I request all the leaders, youth, and the editor of Pashtun newspaper to increase their efforts to awaken their nation by taking the Pashtun newspaper into their hands, and to come to the field with an organized plan for the progress and development of their nation, because the power of the pen alone is not enough to change the current state of the Pashtun; rather, practical action is needed. Therefore, I am personally ready for my efforts in this path and support every action that is for the unity and progress of the Pashtun.

I hope that this Pashtun newspaper of ours will lay the foundation for such a movement that will prove to be a reliable step for solving all the problems of the Pashtuns, and it is the responsibility of every individual to help the Pashtun newspaper for the welfare of their nation, whether it is financially or intellectually.

In the end, I request all Pashtuns to come, let us hold the rope of unity with one hand and fight together to obtain our rights through the Pashtun newspaper for the honor and dignity of our nation, because this is a very great responsibility for our future generations.

215.right: At that time, regarding the celebration of Afghanistan's Independence Day, most of the goods of the Indian merchants of Bareilly were sent for transport, and a committee was appointed to inspect them and determine their rights. This committee finished its work and sent a report through the government office, on behalf of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, to the head of the Bareilly caravan in the name of the committee of Indian merchants of Bareilly. Regarding the receipt of this report, the head of the merchants' committee, who had been informed about this matter by the government on behalf of the government office, wrote in a letter that no specific amount had been indicated for him by the government to act accordingly, and for this, he requested clarification of this matter from the government office through the officials in Kabul. Regarding the office's response to this and their departure, what new and old orders were given by the Afghan government for the Bareilly government, for which the relevant departments prepared new instructions for them and consulted with the relevant departments to carry out this work accordingly, and based on their comprehensive activities, new instructions were issued by the officials in Kabul for the Indian merchants of Bareilly in light of a series of new and old decrees to manage their affairs for this trip.
215.left: At that time, discussions were also underway in the Kabul environment regarding the designation of specific locations for these merchants to sell their goods. In this regard, special measures were taken by the government office to meet with the merchants' representatives in Kabul, so that the ground could be prepared for meetings and the exchange of views to resolve the merchants' problems. In this way, significant steps were taken by the government to regulate the merchants' affairs, which helped in formulating a new policy for the growth and development of trade.

216.right: For some time, there was a major disturbance in the Wardu village of the capital, resulting in casualties, which caused all the shops in the city to be closed for several days, and people were spending their nights in a state of extreme fear and terror. The reason for this major disturbance was that the fire of anger was burning in the hearts of the people against a new action of the British government in Peshawar. People were very angry that the government was conducting searches inside people's homes and paid no attention to preserving their honor and dignity. I remember that when I was traveling towards Quetta, I saw signs of hatred and anger in the eyes of the people along the way. In those days, there were police and military patrols in every corner of the city, and it seemed as if everyone was waiting for a new incident. Amidst all this insecurity and terror, I was trying to find a way to continue my journey so that I could reach my destination safely, but the worsening situation brought my intention to a standstill, and I was forced to postpone the date of my journey.

On the occasion of the publication of "Pashtun" in Kabul

If the Pashtuns in the world want to make their lives equal to others and take steps toward the prosperity and well-being of their lives, then first they must take steps on the path of knowledge and enlightenment. The publication of "Pashtun" is a great victory for the Afghans. This publication will raise the level of knowledge of the Pashtuns and will create love for unity and brotherhood in their hearts. The publication of "Pashtun" will be the beginning of a new dawn among the Afghans. In this publication, much will be written about the progress of the country and the welfare of the people. The publication of this magazine in Kabul is a sign of the Afghan government's love for and efforts toward education. We congratulate all the staff of this publication from the bottom of our hearts and wish them success from God Almighty. We look at this publication with great respect for the unity and prosperity of the Pashtuns.

Question: What is the opinion of the elders regarding the publication of Pashtun?
Answer: The publication of Pashtun is an important decision of the Afghan government.
Question: What is the goal of Pashtun?
Answer: Increasing people's knowledge and the progress of the country.
Question: Is this publication distributed throughout Afghanistan?
Answer: Yes, the goal of this publication is to inform the people of all of Afghanistan.
Question: What do people say about the publication of Pashtun?
Answer: People welcome this publication and see it as a new beginning.

[Regarding the editorial board of the publication]
The leadership of the editorial board is in the hands of Mr. Sardar Sahib. He has made many efforts for the publication of Pashtun. According to him, this publication will be an important tool for spreading unity and knowledge among Afghans. In his opinion, through Pashtun, we will be able to solve our cultural and social problems. The staff of this publication work with great sincerity and in every issue, they try to publish new and useful content. The publication of Pashtun is a source of joy and hope not only in Kabul but throughout Afghanistan.

German News
(By the pen of Mir Rahman (M.A.H) Rajab Mustankar)
Every nation of Europe, according to its power, always creates its influence in Asian
countries. First, they start trade in the country, and then
slowly, under one pretext or another, they quietly subjugate it. However, for the sake of
creating or maintaining this influence, the nations of Europe harbor malice
and jealousy toward one another.
After the Great War, in accordance with this policy, like other Asian
countries, the European nations looked at Iran with greedy eyes. Especially the
Tsarist Russian government. The British and the Germans were making every effort
to create and increase their influence.
Wassmuss was the German government consul in the Iranian port of Bushehr,
under thirty years of age. He was blonde, and his large mustache was a model
of its kind. He had blue eyes, over which large spectacles were always
worn. Along with him was another German consul who was his deputy, and his name
was Dolpman. Wassmuss was young in age, but he was well acquainted with the Iranian language, habits,
customs, and traditions. He had been assigned the task of
instilling love for the Germans and hatred for the British in the hearts of the Iranians.
When the Great War began, this task of Wassmuss became easy
and enjoyable. In the consulate, he would host grand feasts for Iranian leaders and chieftains,
and would bestow upon them valuable gifts.

313.right: In the course of the beginning of a new life and the spread of new ideas in India, the emergence of certain reformist and national newspapers is a clear sign of the awakening of this country. Although these newspapers were under the strict surveillance of the British government, they still kept the love of freedom and national pride alive in the hearts of the people through their pens. Among the Muslims of India, the influence of these publications was greater than others because they were in search of the causes of their destruction and decline. Along with this, news of reformist movements in other countries also reached the people through these newspapers. For example, writings about the changes in Turkey and Egypt brought about a major change in people's thinking. Besides this, some literary and moral topics were also published that played a guiding role for the improvement of society. Although this path was very thorny and there were threats of imprisonment and hardships for many writers, their perseverance and courage caused the lamps of knowledge to be lit in every home and to be used as a powerful weapon against the atrocities of colonialism.
313.left: These newspapers, through a specific style and the use of simple Pashto, conveyed the message of national and political awakening to the minds of the common people. Alongside this, the analysis of historical events and the recounting of experiences from past eras were intended for generations to learn lessons from their mistakes. A major purpose of these writings was for Muslims to unite and save themselves from the politics of division practiced by outsiders. Whenever a writer would write about social corruption or the harms of ignorance, a kind of movement would emerge among the people. In addition to this, important discussions were also held regarding women's education and the upbringing of children. This was, in reality, the beginning of a new era that, through knowledge and enlightenment, sought to roll up the carpet of the dark ages. Furthermore, information about modern sciences and world affairs was also given space in the pages of the newspapers so that readers could take steps in accordance with the demands of the time and not fall behind in this competition.

A story of matches
In the opinion of many people, after the history of creating fire from stone and flint, this is the story of matches, which are now used all over the world to create fire. These matches that we see today have come into existence after many experiments and mistakes. The initial story of these matches is that in 1827, an English chemist named John Walker discovered them. He had used certain things in his experiments to ignite fire, but these matches of his were not very useful. In 1830, a French chemist named Charles Sauria created the first modern match. He had used sulfur and phosphorus, which would ignite upon friction. Regarding this matter in Islam, a Hadith Sharif of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) is as follows: "La tashabbahu bil-kuffar," meaning do not imitate the infidels. In this way, the use of anything that conflicts with our Islamic teachings should be avoided, and we should strive to live according to our Islamic values.

Thanks to his management, knowledge, and honesty, many deserts of Pashtunkhwa have been developed today. The expansion of his scope of work and the reason for his popularity in the hearts of the people is that he is ready for any kind of sacrifice to serve the nation. It is hoped that such services of his will be an excellent torch for the future generation and other young people will also follow in his footsteps.

322.right:
A greeting of brotherhood

For two years, the British government was intent on strictly preventing this, and due to the publication of this article, they had instilled fear in the hearts of the common people; however, despite this, the newspaper was secretly distributed throughout India and was read by people everywhere with great enthusiasm. In those days, this newspaper was an important tool for suppressing the British government.

In 12 months, this newspaper worked with such success for this important goal that it successfully awakened the hearts of the people of India. With the publication of this newspaper, a love for freedom was born among the people, and they stood up against British colonialism.

During the publication of this newspaper, many obstacles were created by the British government, but the newspaper operators faced these obstacles with great courage and remained steadfast on their path. Ultimately, due to the government's severe pressures and bans, the newspaper was eventually closed for some time, but its impact remained lasting in the hearts of the people and paved the way for the freedom movement.
322.left:
A greeting of brotherhood

Understanding and acting upon our own love, brotherhood, and solidarity is something that is essential for every Afghan. This homeland of ours needs unity and accord.

Looking at the recent events that have taken place, it is clear that if we do not become united, we will fall prey to foreign interference. Therefore, it is the duty of every Pashtun to think about their own interests and avoid division.

In the past, we have seen that whenever the enemy wanted to create a rift among us, they used ethnic and linguistic differences. Now the time has come for us to learn from these past experiences and fight for our rights as a single nation.

With the power of the pen, we can raise the level of awareness among the people and warn them of future dangers. The message of brotherhood and solidarity must reach the ears of every village and every home. We must brighten our future in the light of knowledge and wisdom.

323.right: In the past, due to the force of British colonialism, the people of many parts of India were bound in the chains of slavery. At the same time, the people of India launched large-scale freedom movements to gain independence. The British devised various conspiracies to suppress these movements and sowed the seeds of discord among the people, but the valiant nation of India, under the leadership of its leaders, resisted every conspiracy of the British. In this regard, the mention of the (Khilafat Movement) and the (Non-cooperation Movement) is worth noting, which shook the foundations of British autocratic rule. In the end, the continuous struggle of the people of India became the beginning of the end of British colonial rule and paved the way for achieving independence. Studying this historical phase shows us that the unity and solidarity of a nation are essential for defeating any kind of colonialism.
323.left: The contribution of the people of Pashtunkhwa in this struggle is also worth mentioning. Although the British made every effort to consolidate their rule in Pashtunkhwa, they had no choice but to bow down in the face of the sacrifices and devotion of the Pashtuns. The Pashtun leaders, through the unity of their people, stood as a firm bastion against colonialism. They understood that the struggle for freedom is a sacred religious and national duty. In this path, many people sacrificed their lives and many homes were destroyed, but their resolve remained unshaken. Today, as we breathe the air of freedom, it is all the result of the blood and sacrifice of those martyrs and fighters who gave their lives to end colonialism. Therefore, it is necessary to take pride in these golden pages of our history and make the lessons of this struggle of our leaders a torch for the future generation.

Today, as we take a new step in this path, we must think deeply about how we can lay such a foundation for our mother tongue that the future generation will be proud of it. In conclusion, we must say that for the success of this series, the participation of all compatriots, and especially the young generation, is a necessary condition. If we work together, it is not far off that Pashto will achieve a reputable position at the regional level.

The story of the famous thieves of that time (End) The story was such that when those thieves were caught from that area and handed over to the authorities of that time, they were presented in the presence of the ruler of Kabul, and in the course of the investigation of their crimes, they confessed that they had committed many such robberies and murders in various areas of Kabul that had distressed the common people. When the execution order was issued by the government officials after confirming the evidence of their crimes, they were punished for their actions in a large city square in front of the people in great haste, and after that day, the fear and terror of thieves in the city ended.
326.left:

The people also expressed great happiness at this action of the government, and an atmosphere of peace and security was created in the city. After this event, the rate of theft and murder in the city decreased significantly, and the people continued their affairs with peace of mind.

327.right:
January 1919

This is a brief account of the demands and requirements of those two factors of the Islamic state, which the Islamic world, at the beginning of the new century, faced in order to save itself and its religion from this catastrophe, and a brief account of the hidden and open actions of the people of these countries in the face of the deeds of the owners of Islam and its enemies in this path, and how the conditions of the Islamic world were moving and what threats it faced as a result of the waves of change in the countries with the passage of this time.

In those days, when the flames of a world war were spreading among the world's superpowers and each was busy looting Islamic lands to secure its own interests, the biggest problem for Muslims was finding ways to remove the colonialists from this land.

During this era, there was a kind of discord among the leaders of Islamic countries, and they were in competition with each other for their personal interests, which had become the cause of the weakness of the Islamic world and had provided the ground for foreign powers to intervene.

The leaders of the Islamic world should have understood that uniting and creating a strategy for their common interests was the most necessary step to get out of this crisis, and using wisdom in the face of the divisive policies of outsiders was considered a religious and national duty.
327.left:
February 1919

It is worth noting that during this sensitive era, efforts were underway to create a new political map on a global scale, and in this process, decisions were being made regarding the fate of Islamic countries that were not according to their wishes, but were carried out based on the interests of the colonialists, and new maps were being employed to divide them.

There was a need for a society or organization for Muslims that would raise its voice on an international level to defend the interests of the Islamic world, but at that time such a united force did not exist, and the leaders of each country were busy protecting their own limited interests, which was a sign of the beginning of a major catastrophe.

According to historical documents, at that time, most of the Islamic world was under the influence of colonial powers, and they had resorted to religious and ethnic divisions to fulfill their own interests, in order to destroy the unity of Muslims and prolong the life of their colonialism.

In this article, an attempt has been made to examine the actions of the Muslim leaders of that time in light of the political and social conditions of that era and to point out how the need for them to unite against foreign conspiracies was greater than ever.

328.right:
February 1920 AD

Upon hearing the news of the death of Fakhr-e-Afghan, such grief spread among the people of the entire country that tears were flowing from everyone's eyes. At this time, a number of people went to his house and expressed their sorrow regarding this grief; among them were some people who had very close relations with Fakhr-e-Afghan and considered his loss a great tragedy. In this gathering, many people recalled his services and expressed great regret over his death. In the end, his family thanked all the people who shared in their grief during this difficult time and showed sympathy with them.

Some said we should build a memorial for him, others said we should publish a booklet about his work. In this way, the meeting concluded, and everyone had a sense of determination in their hearts to strive for the continuation of his path. Alongside this, ceremonies were held throughout the region to commemorate him, in which the participation of the people was noteworthy.

329.right: The talk of the British leaving India: Nowadays, in every street and bazaar of India, there is heated talk about the British leaving. In the eyes of both Hindus and Muslims, the British are no longer able to stay in India. Although the British are trying to keep this matter hidden from the rest of the world, it has now become a common topic on everyone's lips. This talk of the British leaving is a sign of the awakening of the people of India. The leaders of India are thinking about whose hands the power of India will be in after the British leave. Regarding this matter, a severe disagreement has arisen between the Congress and the Muslim League. Some people say that with the departure of the British, a new era of unrest will begin in India, but another group of people strongly rejects this. In their view, the departure of the British will pave the way for the formation of a free and autonomous government in India. This enthusiasm and passion of the people of India regarding the departure of the British is a manifestation of their love for freedom.
329.left: Regarding the increase in graves: It has become common knowledge regarding the increase in the number of deaths that in many areas the number of graves has increased significantly compared to before. What could be the reason for this? Doctors say that due to poor-quality food, polluted air, and the lack of medical facilities, people's health has been negatively affected. In some places, the spread of epidemics is also considered a major reason for this increase in deaths. Although the government has taken some steps in this regard, much more work is still needed. Ordinary people say that due to the lack of life's amenities, they are facing many difficulties. To improve this situation, it is necessary for the government to take concrete steps in the health sector. This matter of the increase in graves is noteworthy to everyone and it is like a dangerous message for society.

334.right:
Expression of truth

In the course of my literary services, through the articles I have published in the (Afghan) newspaper with the intention of stating facts and awakening my countrymen, a number of people have leveled accusations against me based on their baseless prejudices. In response to the biased comments of these individuals, I say only this: the main goal of my writings is the unity of the Islamic Ummah, the dissemination of knowledge, and speaking the truth against tyranny. In these writings, I have attempted to clarify the actions of those who have tried to pull the wool over people's eyes in the name of religion. Such reactions to my writings are, in reality, a futile attempt to hide the truth that will reveal itself with the passage of time. My pen is not subject to any individual, group, or expediency, nor will it bow down to such threats. I am ready for any sacrifice for the prosperity of my country's citizens, the popularization of education, and the path toward an independent and powerful Afghanistan. If these individuals adopt the path of reason and logic for their criticisms, I will welcome any positive opinion they have, but I will respond to insults and baseless accusations only by stating the truth and reality.
334.left:
The address of the pen's owner

In this article, I have tried to raise my voice regarding the current situation of my country as a person who has committed himself to the path of the nation's freedom and service to the religion. If anyone seeks signs of blasphemy or disrespect for religion in my writings, it is a result of their narrow-mindedness and ignorance of the facts. At first, Kabul University made many efforts in this regard to find a way for the development of the Pashto language. But unfortunately, due to the shortage of Pashto language readers, this task was very difficult. During this time, a group of Pashto scholars and writers emerged and made an effort to take a fundamental step to solve the problems of the Pashto language script. They used new letters for writing the Pashto language and in this way, they brought many changes to the Pashto script. In this process, they also worked hard in collecting Pashto grammar and vocabulary, and thus they greatly enriched Pashto literature and aroused new feelings among the people about the Pashto language, which continues to this day, and they are working for the development of the Pashto language.

During this time, the Kabul Literary Association also played a major role and published many writings and translations for the growth of the Pashto language, which introduced Pashto language enthusiasts to scientific and literary writings.
381.left:
In the course of these efforts for the Pashto language, many efforts were also made to publish the works of famous Pashto poets and writers, so that these works could reach the hands of Pashto language enthusiasts and their level of knowledge could be increased. In this way, with the publication of the works of Pashto writers, a new phase began for the development of Pashto literature, in which many scientific and literary works were written in the Pashto language, and many advancements were made in Pashto literature. Thus, the series of writing and publishing such works in Pashto literature continued, which are now considered an important part of the scientific and literary wealth of the Pashto language.

This is a historical process of the growth and development of the Pashto language, which has seen many changes over the past century. Pashto scholars have made tireless efforts to enrich this language, and today the traces of these efforts are clearly visible in Pashto literature, remaining a great asset for future generations.

383.right:
The Lion and the Tiger
It was early morning, sleep was still in my eyes, and the air was in a state of transition; the sun was beginning to appear slightly over the mountains, the fire was flickering like palm leaves, and the chirping of birds was very loud in every direction, so I also stood up from sleep and went out of my house. I took the path towards the mountains, and while I was walking on the path among the forest trees, sounds were coming from in front of me that made my heart tremble greatly. When I went a little further, I saw in front of me that a tiger was sleeping in the shade of a tree, just like a big old man sleeping carelessly in his sleep. When my heart saw this, I became very afraid and kept my feet very still in place, because if I had made any movement, that tiger would have set his eyes on me, and then escaping from his claws would have been a very difficult task. In the same state, while I was in great fear, another sound came once, which also passed by the tiger's ears, and he woke up from his sleep very quickly and looked towards me. When my eyes met his, all the blood in my body dried up in such a way that I felt like a dead person, and from my heart, I asked God, "O Lord! Save me from this calamity." The tiger also looked at me with a very sharp gaze and, roaring, started running towards me, and I, too, in great fear, started running on my path. In that state, I was praying from my heart, "God, save me from the claws of this tiger." At this time, while I was running very fast, suddenly another sound came, which left me in great surprise; this sound was of another tiger that came from the front and attacked this tiger, and a fight started between the two, so I escaped from that place very quickly and got myself inside the door of my house, and after that day, the fear of such forests remained in my heart, and I never went towards that place again.

384.right:
Moral Education

My thoughts sometimes raise the point that the Pashtun nation in the current era is in dire need of modern education and new sciences, and if the losses that have reached the Pashtun nation because of this are taken into account, then every person with a compassionate heart will admit that the Pashtun nation is in greater need of education at this time than anyone else, and if we do not make efforts within ourselves to spread knowledge and illuminate the light of learning to fulfill this need, then like our past, we will remain backward in this new era as well.

We need to reflect on the fact that what our ancestors did for the progress of our nation in our past times; if we do not reflect on reforming our own conditions ourselves, then who will take the blame for the deterioration of our state?

We also need to act according to those discussions that take place in our homes in favor of education, and finding ways to arrange for the education of our sons and daughters is also in the interest of our nation, so that through it, our nation may walk on the path of prosperity.

It is necessary for us to reflect well on this matter and take such steps for our children that will be the cause of the well-being of their future lives, and we should protect ourselves from such things that become a cause of disgrace in our nation.
384.left:
At this time, if the youth of our nation are pursuing the light of education on one hand, they also need to listen to the words of their elders, which are the result of their experience, because the experience of elders serves as a torch for the future generation.

If we desire the progress of our nation, it is necessary that we step onto the path of unity and agreement among ourselves, and make such efforts to end our internal differences that an atmosphere of unity is created in our nation.

In acquiring education, we need to establish schools and institutions where, along with preserving our religion and civilization, modern sciences are also taught, because by preserving our religion, our morals and our way of life can also be kept on the right path.

In the end, I say that if the Pashtun nation is adorned with the ornament of knowledge, then the day is not far when our nation will stand at the forefront in comparison to other nations of the world, and will become a source of pride for every Pashtun.

It is necessary that work be done with sincerity everywhere to spread this education, and for the achievement of this goal, the self-sacrifice of every Pashtun is also required.

The beauty and curse that is in this saying is not hidden from their view. The truth is this: among animals, the dog is considered the most despicable animal, and generally, its gaze is on detestable things, and it obtains its sustenance in a way that is generally undesirable.

433.right:
The journey of King Amanullah Khan
The intention of the journey from Kabul towards Kandahar became clear from the following discussions, that King Amanullah Khan met with various tribes during his journey and paid attention to listening to their problems and demands. The purpose of King Amanullah Khan's journey was to establish security and unity in different regions of the country and to strengthen close relations with the people. During this journey, King Amanullah Khan also met with the elders of the region and religious scholars and asked them to help in the development of the country. In this journey, King Amanullah Khan also gave some guidance regarding the education and training of the people and emphasized that the development of education is essential for the future of the country. Similarly, to improve the economic situation of the people, he also paid attention to the construction of roads and dams and gave guidance for the solution of their problems.
433.left: In the course of this journey, a new chapter was opened by Shah Amanullah Khan through meeting and interacting with the people, which became a cause for the people's trust. In this journey, Shah Amanullah Khan continued his efforts for the unity of the country's people and conveyed important messages for their national unity. This journey is considered one of the important events in the country's history that reduced the distance between the people and the government and played a significant role in the country's development. At the end of this journey, Shah Amanullah Khan reiterated his commitments for the welfare of the people and called on all the people to unite for the prosperity of the country. This journey brought a new change in the country's politics and created new hopes among the people that the country's future would be bright. The opinions of historians regarding this journey are also that it was a successful journey that strengthened the government's relations with the people and marked the beginning of a new era for the country's development.

He described all the difficulties of his journey and the hardships he had endured for his purpose. Sarkar Sahib was very pleased with his words and told him that there is no problem for me to meet you; you can come at any time. In his gatherings, there was always talk of knowledge and literature, and he looked at everyone with great respect. Although much of his life was spent on important tasks and in the service of the nation, he never showed fatigue when meeting his people. He always tried to listen to people's problems and made efforts to solve them according to his ability. These aspects of his character are still alive in people's hearts today and are worthy of emulation for everyone. It is hoped that this article will be useful for the readers.

A major reason for the decline of Muslims in the field of education is that they do not understand the value of education and do not understand how necessary education is in every aspect of life. It is necessary for the nation to prioritize education.
One thing that hinders the progress of our nation is that we do not fully understand the importance of education. Every member of the nation must understand that we are in a bad situation because of education, and this situation must be changed. Awareness about the value of education must be created among us, and everyone must be given the opportunity to get an education.
In the field of education, the whole nation must unite and make efforts for the advancement of education. If we unite, we can easily make progress in the field of education. In the end, we can say that there is no substitute for education for the progress of the nation, and we must make every kind of sacrifice for education.

Do we rely only on religious sciences, or do we also learn modern sciences? This is a very important question that we must find an answer to.
The role of teachers in the field of education is also very important. Teachers must be qualified and treat students with kindness. Teachers must instill a love for education in the minds of students and must make them understand the value of knowledge.
Besides this, the role of the government is also very important. The government must make efforts for the spread of education and provide facilities for schools and universities. The government must also consider the curriculum of education and create a curriculum that is in accordance with the needs of the nation.
In conclusion, I can say that any kind of negligence in the field of education is not acceptable. We must make every effort for education and must bring our nation out of the darkness of ignorance. Through education, we can give our nation a bright future.

477.right:
Quatrains of Pata Khazana
(Seventh and Eighth Part)
Pata Khazana is a book that contains a biography of ancient Pashtun poets; this book was written by Mohammad Hotak under the order of Shah Hussain Hotak around the year 1142 AH.
Since there were many gaps in the field of Pashto literary history due to the lack of information about the lives and circumstances of old Pashto poets, this book is viewed as an important document of Pashto literary history.
Pata Khazana was first published in Kabul in 1323 SH by the Pashto Academy through the efforts and supervision of Allama Abdul Hai Habibi.
This book is a very valuable treasure of Pashtun literature, through which we can obtain information about the efforts and endeavors of our ancestors in the path of the growth and development of the Pashto language and literature.
Regarding the importance of Pata Khazana, we can say that this book is a fundamental and valuable work not only for the literary history of the Pashtuns but also for understanding the historical process of the Pashto language.
477.left:
In this book, examples of the poetry and life accounts of those Pashtun poets who have had an unforgettable role in the enrichment of the Pashto language have been preserved.
To recognize the value of Pata Khazana, it is necessary to understand its content and the materials contained within it.
This book is a reflection of the deep roots of Pashtun civilization and culture and is considered a strong argument for the proof of the antiquity and richness of the Pashto language.
With the publication of Pata Khazana, many unknown figures of Pashto language and literature were revealed, and Pashto literary history took a step toward a new phase.
In conclusion, it must be said that the preservation of Pata Khazana and the recognition of its content is the duty of every Pashtun, because it is an inseparable part of our identity and history.

510.right: Ultimately, due to the war, which has negatively affected the lives of people in every part of the world in one way or another, a kind of economic turmoil has arisen in our dear homeland, Afghanistan, as in other countries, due to the rise in prices of many items. Therefore, in order for the lives of our people to continue in peace as before, a series of measures are being taken by the government, as a result of which the prices of grain and other essential items will be somewhat lowered and controlled, so that convenience can be created for the general public, because the basic goal of the government is the well-being of its nation and the resolution of their problems. Alongside these efforts by the government, it is necessary for the people to also pay attention to themselves and avoid extravagance in these difficult circumstances. Furthermore, traders are requested to refrain from hoarding and artificially raising the prices of goods, because such actions cause major problems for the general public and are an act contrary to the teachings of the holy religion of Islam. Serious measures will be taken by the government against those who violate these orders, so it is hoped that all compatriots will fully cooperate with the government in this regard in a spirit of national unity so that we can successfully pass through this difficult phase.
510.left: Furthermore, due to hearing news everywhere that people are worried about food shortages and rising prices, government officials are seeking to resolve this problem as quickly as possible and find ways to ensure a sufficient supply of goods in the markets. Some steps have been taken by the government, which include the import of food items and the regulation of their distribution system so that no one faces a shortage of goods. In addition, those who illegally hoard goods and are involved in raising prices will be brought to justice. This is not the first time in our country's history that we have faced such challenges, but the patience and unity of our people have always enabled us to overcome our problems. It is necessary to establish close relations between the government and the people and to avoid any rumors that cause fear and anxiety among the people. We must realize that only through cooperation and patience can we lead our country out of this economic crisis and take steps toward a bright future; it is hoped that all citizens, by realizing this responsibility, will fulfill their national duties.

513.right:
Aristotle

It is often said that the famous sage and ruler was among the sages of the time of Alexander the Great, the emperor of Greece of that time. Although there are many disagreements, his date of birth is shown as 384 BC. Regarding his birth, historians say that his father was a physician at the court of the King of Macedonia. After the death of Aristotle's mother, he was raised by a friend of his father who had a great love for medicine and science. Regarding the beginning of his education and upbringing, it is said that he went to the city of Athens at the age of eighteen and began learning wisdom. He learned from many famous scholars of his time, such as Plato, and benefited greatly from his wisdom. He made so much progress in the fields of philosophy and science that he found a special place among all the scholars of Greece. Alexander the Great, who was the conqueror of all Greek lands, valued Aristotle highly because of his knowledge and the perfection of his wisdom, and used his advice in all matters. Aristotle spent most of his life in scientific work and in the service of spreading Greek knowledge.

519.right:
Regarding the truth of the Kabul meeting

Regarding the truth of the Kabul meeting, in continuation of our discussions in previous issues in response to the objections of some people regarding the Kabul meeting, another point is worth mentioning. That is, some people were divided into different groups regarding this meeting, and this was spread in various ways by those who did not have information about the meeting. The origin of this matter is that when the idea of holding this meeting first arose, there was no disagreement whatsoever. But later, when some people saw their interests in it, they tried to sow seeds of discord in it with various pretexts. The main perpetrators of this were those who wanted to create disunity among the people in this way and to exploit the structure of the meeting for their own ends. In any case, it is very bad for a society to have so much disunity on an important issue. We must refrain from such actions and work for unity.
519.left:
Brother Ali Muhammad Sahib

May it be full of goodness and blessings

Looking at the past months, it is also necessary to mention another topic regarding this meeting in Kabul. When the news of holding this meeting in Kabul was officially spread among the people, it was spread by a group that this meeting was held for a specific purpose. But the truth is that the purpose of this meeting was solely and solely to find a common path for the good and welfare of the country and the nation. Some people who took the path of opposition due to the absence of their personal interests in this meeting tried to create doubts among the people. Instead of working for unity, they created an atmosphere of distrust among the participants of the meeting through very low tactics. While all the participants of the meeting understood how much unity is valuable for the benefit of the country. I hope that our countrymen will not be deceived by the words of such people and instead of wasting their time in differences, they will take steps towards unity and brotherhood. It is the duty of every Afghan to work for unity and stop such people who sow the seeds of discord.

Although this movement may seem to some as a form of confrontation with the government, the truth is that its purpose is not to confront the government, but rather to express a new thought and vision for the preservation of the nation's rights and for its progress and development. At the same time, it must be kept in mind how essential it is to maintain order and discipline during such movements, so that no obstacles arise in the path of fulfilling the people's aspirations. If this movement is carried forward in a proper and organized manner, it will certainly reach its desired results and will be a major step toward solving the nation's problems. In the same way, as a result of such efforts, people will also have the opportunity to realize the importance of unity and mutual assistance, which is the primary condition for the survival and progress of every nation.

In the current circumstances, the difficulties and problems that have arisen are all the result of our disunity and lack of cooperation with one another. If we want to get rid of all these problems, the only way is for us to find unity among ourselves and work with one hand and one heart for our national interests. It is the duty of our leaders to encourage people in this direction and make them understand the value of unity, so that the whole nation can fight together for one goal. For this, we must make efforts to increase knowledge, wisdom, and education, because the foundation of a nation's progress and development rests on education. In the end, we must say that if we perform our responsibility properly today, we will leave a bright and prosperous life for future generations, and this will be a great service for the pride of our nation.

523.right:
News

When the idea of establishing a pharmacy in Kabul for the distribution of medicines came to the mind of this humble friend, he started the work by renting a shop for the first time. At that time, people criticized him a lot and said that this was not a job for common people, but this humble friend did not care about these words and continued his work. At that time, he managed to raise the money needed for the shop with great difficulty; he borrowed some money from his father and started his work by setting up a small pharmacy. At that time, there were many difficulties regarding medicines in Kabul, and people were very distressed. This humble friend worked day and night in the service of the people. In this pharmacy, medicines for all kinds of diseases were available for the people. If someone did not have the money for medicine, he would give it to them for free. This action of his became a great source of benefit for the people; people praised this service of his and thanked him very much. This humble friend also provided space for doctors in this pharmacy so that they could examine patients. This action of his was a very great service for the people of Kabul. In a short time, his pharmacy became a source of hope for the people. People from everywhere came to his pharmacy and bought medicine for their illnesses. This humble friend gained a lot of profit from this pharmacy and made great progress in his life. This is the story of a person who, through his efforts, was able to serve the people and succeed in the path of his life.
523.left:
News

When the work of building schools for the spread of education began in the city of Kabul, this humble friend made great efforts for this work. He started preaching among the people of Kabul for the sake of learning education. He would tell people that education is a duty for everyone; if you want to improve your life, then step onto the path of education. With these speeches of his, the fire of love for learning education was ignited in the hearts of the people. This work of his also became very valuable to the rulers of the time; they considered his work very useful for the development of education and gave him land to build schools. This humble friend made efforts to build schools in very difficult circumstances. When the schools were built, the people's respect and appreciation for him increased greatly. People saw this work of his as a bright lamp for their future. This humble friend did many things to serve the people throughout his life, and these works of his remained on the pages of history forever.

History, and higher sciences such as Tafsir, Hadith, Fiqh, Usul al-Fiqh, Kalam, and Tasawwuf were acquired. In these disciplines, his teachers were the top scholars of Afghanistan, one of whom was a master named Bin Ali. After these books, Sayyid Sahib also read famous Islamic books. Sayyid Sahib's efforts were focused on books of philosophy and religious studies.

At the age of eighteen, after acquiring these sciences, Sayyid Sahib went to India in 1842. After leaving Afghanistan, he read books and learned wisdom (Hikmat) in India, and he also studied mathematics and wisdom in the Arab style.

In this meeting, it was decided to form the Pashtun "Zalmo Jirga" (Youth Jirga), similar to the "All India Youth League" group in India. The basic purpose of forming this Jirga was to show Pashtuns the path of national unity, independence, and the struggle for their rights. In this meeting, Pashtun leaders emphasized in their speeches that Pashtuns must adopt the path of unity and strive for a common goal. The leaders of this Jirga told the participants of the meeting that without unity, Pashtuns cannot achieve their rights and for this purpose, they must support each other in all circumstances. Likewise, decisions were also made in this meeting to strengthen the cultural and social affairs of the Pashtuns. It is worth mentioning that the message of unity was spread in the meetings of this Jirga and it guided the Pashtuns to rise as a united force. I say amen to this statement of my Pashtun brothers of the American nation, who give a lot of money in the path of noble service and love!

The truth is that today, work cannot be done without money. You see, today, any nation that does not have a strong treasury cannot have new propaganda, hospitals, and schools for its nation, and cannot serve the country and religion of its people; and if a nation does not have a treasury, then you see that it is equal to nothing else, which is the state of the nation.

If a person asks why Pashtuns do not do as other nations do, this statement is wrong; Pashtuns give much more charity than their means. But their method of charity is such that it provides no immediate benefit to the nation, it is not eternal; undoubtedly, their method of charity is in the form of the past era, but today this benefit is a loss to the nation.

The era has changed; it was necessary for Muslims to have changed too. But they did not change with the era, because instead of benefit, it is a loss for them. In the past, people would serve the nation and religion for free, and you would collect money for the people, give it to them, and in this way, the service of the nation continued, and the servants also managed to survive.

But you see today that everything is for money. The era has changed; propaganda, publication, school, imamate—in fact, there is no matter that can be done without money, and no such person will die who girds his loins to serve the nation for the sake of God. If a person girds his loins, if he is wealthy, like our Pashtuns, he will manage, but if he is poor, then what?

For this reason, today it is necessary for Muslims to move with the pace of the era, for Pashtuns to form a national treasury with unity like other nations for money, meat, and cash ideas, and to help the nation, and to remove the poverty of the nation, and to support the servants of Islam. O Pashtuns! How many innocent people were arrested and put in jail by the government? And what kind of cruelties were inflicted upon the poor people of the village? Why was this done? What was the fault of the youth? Truly, you will be surprised that this is not the place, the government does not listen to the truth. So, O Pashtun brothers, what was our fault that such excess was committed against us?
The truth is that the rulers do not want this spirit to be born among us Pashtuns—that we should call right as right and wrong as wrong to the government. The rulers say that whatever the youth order, people should not trust them. You might say that today people talk about this, but the rulers tell them otherwise. O brothers! Times have changed. You must know that today in England, there is a rule of the laborers; that is, the power and authority of the kingdom are in the hands of the laborers. However, it is a historical fact that in the great assembly (Parliament) of England, a man proposed that laborers should also be given some rights in this assembly. So, I ask you, what treatment did he receive? He was hanged, but today the laborers have the right, and today their rule has been established.
O Pashtun brothers! The world is changing, and it has changed. But this is not just for us; I say to you that the path of Abbas Khan, and the path of Abbas Khan, in which we are stuck in those customs, traditions, and prejudices—that is finished. It was necessary for Abbas Khan to leave Pashtun traditions and prejudices. Wake up, brothers, and recognize your nation, and leave them. Stand up, or else we will be destroyed.
After the month of Ramadan, we all came to the Charsadda Tehsil, and there was a strange situation in the government. Then, from Charsadda, everyone else was released, and I was left alone in those circumstances.
When it became evening, my own guard told me about the situation. I asked why the food was not brought from the village. It became clear that Mr. Willy, I.C.S., who was the assistant at that time, had ordered it a few days ago. We also had a seventh arrangement; it was closed. I was surprised as to why it would have been closed. The guard himself came to me, and it became known that some police officers had given permission for the guard to enter. I was grateful for their kindness and sympathy. I thought that perhaps the police officers had complained to the Sahib, saying, "Sahib, this is a poor man; his salary is low, and he is barely making ends meet; he is a brother-like friend." But I still treated them well, and I politely refused all their bribes. I replied to them, "I do not eat the hunger of bribes. Look, you will hear from me again." And I closed the food. I see that the next day, Willy Sahib came. I asked him what the reason was for closing the food. He replied that the day I was releasing Abbas Khan, he had come to see the situation.

February 1930

Congress Session in Lahore

The Congress is an assembly of the Hindus, Muslims, Sikhs, Parsis, and Christians of India. Once a year, this session is held in one of the provinces of India, and people from all over India gather there. The work of this assembly is to liberate our country (India) from foreigners. These people strive day and night, thinking of ways by which we can be freed from the slavery of foreigners.

This year's session was held in Lahore. Many foreigners from America, Germany, and Britain came to observe it. It is a pity that although this session was so close to our frontier, very few people from the Pashtun region participated.

What should I say about this session, and if I were to describe it in detail, this entire magazine of mine would be filled, and there would be no room left for other articles. Even then, the joy and understanding that I experienced would not be fully conveyed. Therefore, I wish to present only the essential points of this session for your service.

You must be aware that many efforts are being made by this assembly. The British have given us some rights, but since this is our country, it is necessary that we have some share in the government. ---

We praise Him and seek His help and pray upon His noble Messenger. As for what follows!
I have come to preside over this meeting with firm determination from my heart, and I express my gratitude with sincere heart. In those nations that have attained political freedom, their industry, craft, and trade are not fully bound by chains and shackles. In their education, too, many changes occur at every stage. During the era of India's slavery, the educational system that exists in our present day was very different from the education of that time. At that time, the number of schools was high, and we cannot find a single example or model in this current time of scholars and learned men like Abul Fazl, Faizi, Timurmal, Urfi, Ghalib, Zauqi, and many others whose names are known to every person.

But brothers! If you agree that we are slaves and the demand of our honor is that we free ourselves from slavery and our honor be restored, then what proposal do you consider appropriate for this? Do you hope that a power will come from the unseen and set us free? Or is it not necessary to make an effort ourselves? In my opinion, those who are not even ready to talk about this effort, how will they achieve the freedom of the country? Effort is necessary in any case, and now the question is not just effort, but the unanimous effort of the entire nation. So now the question arises, what method of effort is necessary? As I have thought about it, I see two ways that people use to achieve freedom. One way is to prefer obedience to the government; the principles of this method are to salute the government's door for one's demands and to ask for one's goals through begging and pleading. This method has proven to be wrong, because for about forty years, this path has been chosen, no benefit has been gained from it, and the whole world has accepted that the British government does not give anything to anyone through begging and pleading. The second way is the one that most nations of the world have chosen to achieve freedom, and most have succeeded through this path. That is war with weapons, facing others with swords, answering a gun with a gun, and a cannon with a cannon. This method is considered a cause of success for other nations, but for the people of India, this method is not successful, because the people of India have neither weapons nor the skill to use them. For us, there is a third way, and that is unity, so that all people become one in hand and heart and, with consensus, confront the government for their rights.

There is a third way that we must try, and remember that abstinence means not becoming like others, like strangers, and in every task where we fight for our rights, we must stand for our goals with courage and the audacity of self-sacrifice. The effort for freedom succeeds when the spirit of unity, brotherhood, and mutual assistance is born within it. The British government has ignited the fire of discord between ourselves and others to scatter the people of India. We must protect ourselves from this fire and extend a hand of companionship and brotherhood to one another in every hardship. If we do this, then it is certain that as a result, the path to India's freedom will be paved, and we will be freed from the chains of this slavery. For this, it is necessary that we turn toward education, because through knowledge we will recognize our rights and find the path of struggle to obtain our rights. May God Almighty grant us the ability to struggle together for the freedom of our country.

675.right:
Readers, it is hoped that it will continue until such time as it finds the success it deserves.
I consider it appropriate to present a request to my dear ones in your service.
First, you are aware of how much newspapers and magazines are needed for the progress of a nation; the conditions of living nations will provide you with the answer to this.
That is, for those nations that are developed today, it is known to you how many of their magazines and newspapers are in circulation; rather, it would be more appropriate to say that whatever progress a nation makes, it is greatly aided by newspapers and magazines.
My second request is whether you want our country to progress. If you do, can only one monthly magazine be sufficient for a great nation and a great country, and will its life depend solely on the support of one person? If I believe in that awakening among you, which you have achieved thanks to last year's political movement, then now is the time for us to develop our newspaper like other nations, change 'Pashtun' from a magazine into a newspaper format, and incorporate into it those qualities that we see in the newspapers of the present era. Such as:
(1) Its printing and paper should be much better than the current state.
(2) Publication should be at least once a week instead of monthly (weekly).
(3) It should include pictures, organization, and order—because in this day and age, the general public has a great interest in pictures.
(4) Capable article writers should be included in its staff, so that 'Pashtun' may be considered a high-level academic newspaper. In short, the effort should be made for 'Pashtun' to become beautiful again, both outwardly and inwardly.
So, readers! You know that all these qualities depend on one word from you.

In the meantime, the Government of India took a number of measures in light of the Viceroy's talks to create some new hope among the people, but these measures were also not sufficient to solve all the problems of the people. Regarding these actions of the Viceroy, there were various opinions among the people of India; some people supported the Viceroy's actions, while others were suspicious of the Viceroy's intentions. In any case, for the people of India, the path of dialogue with the Viceroy was the best way for their problems to be resolved peacefully.
